nodes.description: Public mapping(address=>uint) tracking token balances; mutated in transferFrom and batchSend without SafeMath.
Public nested mapping(address=>mapping(address=>uint)) of spending allowances; mutated in approve and transferFrom.
Private owner address set in the constructor to msg.sender; the sole access-control anchor for privileged functions.
Address whitelisted for trading; writable by owner via setTradeAddress and read in ensure.
Maximum number of sells per address, configured in init and read in condition.
Minimum sale amount threshold, configured in init and read in condition.
Maximum sale amount threshold, configured in init and read in condition.
Per-address sale counter, incremented in transferFrom and read in condition.
Mapping(address=>bool) of addresses allowed to sell without further checks; read in ensure.
Public total supply, set once in the constructor.
Caller-controlled origin/identity used for allowance spending, ownership checks and balance transfers.
Public payable entry point that forwards execution to transferFrom(msg.sender,_to,_value).
Core transfer routine: spends allowance, calls ensure/condition gating, mutates balanceOf and _onSaleNum.
Whitelist gate reading owner, UNI pair, tradeAddress and canSale, then enforcing condition(_from,_value).
Sets allowance[msg.sender][_spender] to an arbitrary caller-supplied value.
Sale-limit validation reading _saleNum, _minSale, _maxSale and _onSaleNum.
Owner-only function performing an arbitrary delegatecall to address a with calldata b.
Owner-only initialization of _saleNum, _minSale and _maxSale values.
Owner-only batch distribution looping over recipients and mutating balanceOf with unchecked arithmetic.
Owner-only setter for the tradeAddress whitelist entry.
Pure function deriving a Uniswap pair address from factory/token hashes; called by ensure.
Deployer sets name, symbol, totalSupply, owner = msg.sender and mints the full supply.
Low-level delegatecall to a caller/owner-supplied address executing arbitrary code in the token's storage context.
Unchecked multiplication/multiplication-independent balance mutations in batchSend (total = _value * _tos.length, balanceOf updates) without SafeMath.
Raw allowance[_from][msg.sender] -= _value subtraction performed without SafeMath in transferFrom.
Recipient address argument of transfer/transferFrom.
Token amount argument supplied by the caller.
Source address argument of transferFrom.
Spender address argument of approve.
Array of recipient addresses passed to batchSend.
Target contract address passed to delegate.
Raw calldata payload passed to delegate/delegatecall.
Sale count limit argument of init.
Minimum sale token amount argument of init.
Maximum sale token amount argument of init.
Local computed as _value * _tos.length in batchSend.
Loop-local recipient address indexed from _tos in batchSend.
Local Uniswap pair address derived by pairFor inside ensure.
New trade address argument of setTradeAddress.

edges.reason: msg.sender is passed as _from into transfer, making the caller the source of funds and establishing caller-controlled identity.
transfer forwards its arguments to transferFrom, propagating caller and value data into the core transfer routine.
transferFrom reads and decrements the allowance mapping when the caller is not the source address.
transferFrom debits balanceOf[_from] and credits balanceOf[_to], directly mutating token balances.
transferFrom is gated by require(ensure(_from,_to,_value)), so execution depends on the whitelist check.
transferFrom performs the unchecked allowance subtraction at operation node 24 when spending allowance.
The unchecked subtraction writes the reduced allowance back into the allowance mapping without SafeMath.
ensure calls pairFor to compute the Uniswap pair address used in the whitelist comparison.
ensure compares _from/_to against owner, allowing owner addresses to bypass all sale restrictions.
ensure requires condition(_from,_value) for non-whitelisted addresses, delegating sale-limit validation.
delegate unconditionally reaches the arbitrary delegatecall operation after the owner check passes.
delegate validates msg.sender == owner, so caller identity controls access to privileged code execution.
delegate reads the owner state variable for its authorization check.
delegatecall transfers execution to external untrusted code that runs in the token's storage context.
The caller-supplied bytes payload b is used directly as delegatecall calldata.
init enforces require(msg.sender == owner), making caller identity the sole gate.
init reads the owner variable to authorize sale parameter configuration.
batchSend checks msg.sender == owner before distributing balances.
batchSend reads owner for its authorization require.
batchSend computes total = _value * _tos.length and mutates balances using unchecked arithmetic.
The unchecked operations decrement the sender balance and increment recipient balances in balanceOf.
setTradeAddress requires msg.sender == owner before changing the whitelist.
setTradeAddress reads owner to validate the privileged setter call.
setTradeAddress writes the supplied address into the tradeAddress whitelist variable.
The constructor assigns owner = msg.sender, seeding all subsequent access control.
The constructor writes the owner state variable and mints the full supply to it.
approve writes allowance[msg.sender][_spender], letting any caller grant arbitrary allowances over their own balance.
approve assigns the caller-supplied amount into the allowance mapping.
condition reads _saleNum to compare against _onSaleNum[_from].
condition reads _minSale to enforce a minimum transfer value.
condition reads _maxSale to enforce a maximum transfer value.
condition reads the per-address sale counter _onSaleNum[_from].
ensure reads tradeAddress as part of its whitelist bypass conditions.
ensure reads the canSale mapping to grant whitelisted addresses free transfers.
The _to parameter flows into transfer and onward into the transfer routine.
The _value parameter flows into transfer and controls the moved amount.
The _from parameter flows directly into transferFrom's balance and allowance logic.
The _spender parameter is written into the allowance mapping by approve.
The _tos array parameter is iterated by batchSend to select balance recipients.
The address parameter a is the delegatecall target in delegate.
The saleNum parameter is stored into the _saleNum state variable by init.
The token parameter is scaled and stored into _minSale by init.
The maxToken parameter is scaled and stored into _maxSale by init.
The local total computed in batchSend determines the sender balance debit.
_value * _tos.length is an unchecked multiplication feeding the unsafe balance mutation.
The loop-local _to receives each array element in batchSend's distribution loop.
Each loop-local recipient is credited via unchecked balanceOf[_to] += _value.
The locally derived _UNI pair address is compared against _from inside ensure.
The addr parameter supplied to setTradeAddress becomes the new tradeAddress value.

normalization_plan.reason: The recipient parameter only exists as input to the transfer/transferFrom entry point and should be folded into the owning function node.
The amount parameter is consumed by the core transfer logic and is not a standalone semantic unit.
The source-address parameter is only meaningful inside transferFrom's allowance and balance updates.
The spender argument only exists to populate the allowance mapping inside approve.
The recipient array is a transient input iterated solely by the batchSend distribution loop.
The target address parameter is only used as the delegatecall destination.
The raw calldata payload is consumed directly by the delegatecall unsafe operation.
The sale-count argument is immediately stored by init and has no independent meaning.
The minimum-sale argument is scaled and written by init only.
The maximum-sale argument is scaled and written by init only.
The local total is the product of unchecked multiplication feeding the unsafe balance debit.
The loop-local recipient is a temporary iteration variable inside batchSend.
The derived pair address exists only for ensure's whitelist comparison.
The address argument is a transient input immediately written into tradeAddress.
